sanskrit: anīkayoḥ saṃhatayor yadīyād brāhmaṇo 'ntarā śāntim icchann ubhayato na yoddhavyaṃ tadā bhavet maryādāṃ śāśvatīṃ bhindyād brāhmaṇaṃ yo 'bhilaṅghayet
english: If, when two armies stand arrayed against each other, a brāhmaṇa should pass between them desiring peace from both sides, then there must be no fighting; whoever transgresses against that brāhmaṇa breaks an eternal bound.

sanskrit: atha cel laṅghayed enāṃ maryādāṃ kṣatriyabruvaḥ apraśasyas tad ūrdhvaṃ syād anādeyaś ca saṃsadi
english: And if one who merely calls himself a kṣatriya should overstep this bound, he shall thereafter be without honor, and his word shall carry no weight in the assembly.

sanskrit: yā tu dharmavilopena maryādābhedanena ca tāṃ vṛttiṃ nānuvarteta vijigīṣur mahīpatiḥ dharmalabdhād dhi vijayāt ko lābho 'bhyadhiko bhavet
english: The king who would conquer should not pursue any course that destroys dharma and shatters the bounds; for what gain could be greater than a victory won in accord with dharma?

sanskrit: sahasā nāmya bhūtāni kṣipram eva prasādayet sāntvena bhogadānena sa rājñāṃ paramo nayaḥ
english: Having swiftly bent the people to his will, he should quickly win them over with conciliation and the granting of enjoyments: this is the highest policy of kings.

sanskrit: bhujyamānā hy ayogena svarāṣṭrād abhitāpitāḥ amitrān paryupāsīran vyasanaughapratīkṣiṇaḥ
english: For those who are exploited without justice, scorched within their own realm, will turn to attend upon his enemies, awaiting the flood of his misfortunes.

sanskrit: amitropagrahaṃ cāsya te kuryuḥ kṣipram āpadi saṃduṣṭāḥ sarvato rājan rājavyasanakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
english: And in his hour of distress they would swiftly side with the foe, O king—wholly disaffected and longing for the king's ruin.

sanskrit: nāmitro vinikartavyo nāticchedyaḥ kathaṃ cana jīvitaṃ hy apy aticchinnaḥ saṃtyajaty ekadā naraḥ
english: An enemy must never be utterly mutilated nor pressed past all bearing; for a man pressed too far will one day cast away his very life.

sanskrit: alpenāpi hi saṃyuktas tuṣyaty evāparādhikaḥ śuddhaṃ jīvitam evāpi tādṛśo bahu manyate
english: Even the wrongdoer, granted some little thing, is content; and one in such straits prizes even his bare life highly.

sanskrit: yasya sphīto janapadaḥ saṃpannaḥ priyarājakaḥ saṃtuṣṭabhṛtyasacivo dṛḍhamūlaḥ sa pārthivaḥ
english: He whose realm is thriving and prosperous, whose king is beloved, whose servants and ministers are content—that ruler stands firm-rooted.

sanskrit: ṛtvikpurohitācāryā ye cānye śrutasaṃmatāḥ pūjārhāḥ pūjitā yasya sa vai lokajid ucyate
english: He by whom the officiating priests, the household chaplain, the teachers, and all others esteemed for sacred learning—those worthy of honor—are duly honored, he indeed is called a conqueror of the worlds.

sanskrit: etenaiva ca vṛttena mahīṃ prāpa surottamaḥ anv eva caindraṃ vijayaṃ vyajigīṣanta pārthivāḥ
english: By this very conduct the foremost of the gods won the earth; and following Indra's victory, kings too have sought to conquer.

sanskrit: bhūmivarjaṃ puraṃ rājā jitvā rājānam āhave amṛtāś cauṣadhīḥ śaśvad ājahāra pratardanaḥ
english: Having vanquished a king in battle, Pratardana seized the conquered city but spared its land, and carried off again and again its life-giving healing herbs.

sanskrit: agnihotrāṇy agniśeṣaṃ havir bhājanam eva ca ājahāra divodāsas tato viprakṛto 'bhavat
english: Divodāsa carried off the sacred fires, the remnants of the fire, the oblations, and the very sacrificial vessels; therefore he came to be reviled.

sanskrit: sarājakāni rāṣṭrāṇi nābhāgo dakṣiṇāṃ dadau anyatra śrotriyasvāc ca tāpasasvāc ca bhārata
english: Nābhāga gave away whole kingdoms together with their kings as sacrificial fee, save only the property of vedic scholars and of ascetics, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: uccāvacāni vṛttāni dharmajñānāṃ yudhiṣṭhira āsan rājñāṃ purāṇānāṃ sarvaṃ tan mama rocate
english: Manifold and varied, O Yudhiṣṭhira, were the ways of the ancient kings who knew dharma; and all of it is approved by me.

sanskrit: sarvavidyātirekād vā jayam icchen mahīpatiḥ na māyayā na dambhena ya icched bhūtim ātmanaḥ
english: Or let the king who desires his own prosperity seek victory through surpassing mastery of every branch of knowledge—never through deceit, never through fraud.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kṣatradharmān na pāpīyān dharmo 'sti bharatarṣabha abhiyāne ca yuddhe ca rājā hanti mahājanam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: There is no dharma more grievous than the dharma of the kṣatriya, O bull of the Bhāratas, for in marching forth and in battle the king destroys a great multitude of people.

sanskrit: atha sma karmaṇā yena lokāñ jayati pārthivaḥ vidvañ jijñāsamānāya prabrūhi bharatarṣabha
english: Then tell me, O learned one, O bull of the Bhāratas, to me who longs to know: by what deed does a king win the higher worlds?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca nigraheṇa ca pāpānāṃ sādhūnāṃ pragraheṇa ca yajñair dānaiś ca rājāno bhavanti śucayo 'malāḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: By the restraint of the wicked and the support of the good, by sacrifices and by gifts, kings become pure and free of stain.

sanskrit: uparundhanti rājāno bhūtāni vijayārthinaḥ ta eva vijayaṃ prāpya vardhayanti punaḥ prajāḥ
english: Kings bent on conquest press hard upon living beings; yet those same kings, once victory is won, make their subjects flourish again.

sanskrit: apavidhyanti pāpāni dānayajñatapobalaiḥ anugraheṇa bhūtānāṃ puṇyam eṣāṃ pravardhate
english: They cast off their sins by the power of gift, sacrifice, and austerity; and through their grace toward living beings their merit grows.

sanskrit: yathaiva kṣetranirdātā nirdan vai kṣetram ekadā hinasti kakṣaṃ dhānyaṃ ca na ca dhānyaṃ vinaśyati
english: Just as a weeder of a field, weeding it once, destroys the brush together with the grain, yet the grain itself is not lost—

sanskrit: evaṃ śastrāṇi muñcanto ghnanti vadhyān athaikadā tasyaiṣā niṣkṛtiḥ kṛtsnā bhūtānāṃ bhāvanaṃ punaḥ
english: so those who loose their weapons slay, on one occasion, those fit to be slain; and the full atonement for that is the fostering of living beings thereafter.

sanskrit: yo bhūtāni dhanajyānād vadhāt kleśāc ca rakṣati dasyubhyaḥ prāṇadānāt sa dhanadaḥ sukhado virāṭ
english: He who protects living beings from loss of wealth, from slaughter, and from affliction, and saves their lives from robbers—he is a giver of wealth, a giver of happiness, a sovereign in splendor.

sanskrit: sa sarvayajñair ījāno rājāthābhayadakṣiṇaiḥ anubhūyeha bhadrāṇi prāpnotīndrasalokatām
english: That king, having sacrificed with all the sacrifices whose fee is the gift of fearlessness, enjoys blessings here and attains to dwelling in the same world as Indra.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇārthe samutpanne yo 'bhiniḥsṛtya yudhyate ātmānaṃ yūpam ucchritya sa yajño 'nantadakṣiṇaḥ
english: When a cause arises for the sake of the brāhmaṇas, he who marches forth and fights, raising his own self as the sacrificial post—his is a sacrifice of boundless fee.

sanskrit: abhīto vikirañ śatrūn pratigṛhṇañ śarāṃs tathā na tasmāt tridaśāḥ śreyo bhuvi paśyanti kiṃ cana
english: Fearless, scattering his foes and likewise receiving their arrows—the gods behold nothing on earth more excellent than such a man.

sanskrit: tasya yāvanti śastrāṇi tvacaṃ bhindanti saṃyuge tāvataḥ so 'śnute lokān sarvakāmaduho 'kṣayān
english: As many weapons as pierce his skin in the fray, so many imperishable worlds does he enjoy, yielding every desire.

sanskrit: na tasya rudhiraṃ gātrād āvedhebhyaḥ pravartate sa ha tenaiva raktena sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
english: The blood that flows from the wounds of his body is no defilement; rather, by that very blood he is released from all his sins.

sanskrit: yāni duḥkhāni sahate vraṇānām abhitāpane na tato 'sti tapo bhūya iti dharmavido viduḥ
english: Whatever pains he endures in the searing of his wounds—there is no austerity greater than that, so the knowers of dharma have understood.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhato bhīravaḥ saṃkhye vartante 'dhamapūruṣāḥ śūrāc charaṇam icchantaḥ parjanyād iva jīvanam
english: In the rear of the battle linger the cowards, the basest of men, seeking shelter from the brave man as one seeks life-giving rain from the cloud.

sanskrit: yadi śūras tathā kṣeme pratirakṣet tathā bhaye pratirūpaṃ janāḥ kuryur na ca tad vartate tathā
english: If the brave man would shield them in safety as he does in danger, men would render him fitting honor—yet it does not work out so.

sanskrit: yadi te kṛtam ājñāya namaskuryuḥ sadaiva tam yuktaṃ nyāyyaṃ ca kuryus te na ca tad vartate tathā
english: If they, knowing what he has done, would always bow to him and act toward him with fitness and justice—but it does not work out so.

sanskrit: puruṣāṇāṃ samānānāṃ dṛśyate mahad antaram saṃgrāme 'nīkavelāyām utkruṣṭe 'bhipatatsu ca
english: Among men seemingly equal a great difference is seen in battle, at the hour when the ranks clash, amid the war-cries and the charging onset.

sanskrit: pataty abhimukhaḥ śūraḥ parān bhīruḥ palāyate āsthāyāsvargyam adhvānaṃ sahāyān viṣame tyajan
english: The brave man falls facing the foe; the coward flees, taking a road that leads not to heaven, abandoning his comrades in the moment of peril.

sanskrit: mā sma tāṃs tādṛśāṃs tāta janiṣṭhāḥ puruṣādhamān ye sahāyān raṇe hitvā svastimanto gṛhān yayuḥ
english: Never beget such men, my son—those basest of men who, abandoning their comrades in battle, went home unscathed and pleased with themselves.

sanskrit: asvasti tebhyaḥ kurvanti devā indrapurogamāḥ tyāgena yaḥ sahāyānāṃ svān prāṇāṃs trātum icchati
english: The gods, with Indra at their head, work woe upon them—those who by deserting their comrades seek to save their own lives.

sanskrit: taṃ hanyuḥ kāṣṭhaloṣṭair vā daheyur vā kaṭāgninā paśuvan mārayeyur vā kṣatriyā ye syur īdṛśāḥ
english: Such a man the kṣatriyas should strike down with sticks and clods, or burn with a fire of straw, or slaughter like a beast—those kṣatriyas who are of true worth.

sanskrit: adharmaḥ kṣatriyasyaiṣa yac chayyāmaraṇaṃ bhavet visṛjañ śleṣmapittāni kṛpaṇaṃ paridevayan
english: This is the kṣatriya's disgrace: that his death should come upon a bed, spilling phlegm and bile, wailing piteously.

sanskrit: avikṣatena dehena pralayaṃ yo 'dhigacchati kṣatriyo nāsya tat karma praśaṃsanti purāvidaḥ
english: The kṣatriya who meets his dissolution with body unwounded—those who know the ancient lore do not praise that act of his.

sanskrit: na gṛhe maraṇaṃ tāta kṣatriyāṇāṃ praśasyate śauṭīrāṇām aśauṭīram adharmyaṃ kṛpaṇaṃ ca tat
english: Death at home, my son, is not commended for kṣatriyas; for the proud, that is ignoble, contrary to dharma, and wretched.

sanskrit: idaṃ duḥkham aho kaṣṭaṃ pāpīya iti niṣṭanan pratidhvastamukhaḥ pūtir amātyān bahu śocayan
english: "Ah, this is pain, this is anguish, this is the bitterest of woes"—so groaning, his face wasted away, his body foul, causing much grief to his ministers—

sanskrit: arogāṇāṃ spṛhayate muhur mṛtyum apīcchati vīro dṛpto 'bhimānī ca nedṛśaṃ mṛtyum arhati
english: he envies the healthy and again and again longs even for death; the hero, proud and high of spirit, deserves no such death as this.

sanskrit: raṇeṣu kadanaṃ kṛtvā jñātibhiḥ parivāritaḥ tīkṣṇaiḥ śastraiḥ suvikliṣṭaḥ kṣatriyo mṛtyum arhati
english: Having wrought havoc in battle, ringed by his kinsmen, sorely torn by keen weapons—such a death the kṣatriya deserves.

sanskrit: śūro hi satyamanyubhyām āviṣṭo yudhyate bhṛśam kṛtyamānāni gātrāṇi parair naivāvabudhyate
english: For the brave man, possessed by truth and righteous wrath, fights fiercely, and does not even feel his limbs being hewn apart by his foes.

sanskrit: sa saṃkhye nidhanaṃ prāpya praśastaṃ lokapūjitam svadharmaṃ vipulaṃ prāpya śakrasyaiti salokatām
english: Meeting his end in battle—an end lauded and honored by the world—having fulfilled his own ample dharma, he attains to dwelling in the world of Śakra.

sanskrit: sarvo yodhaḥ paraṃ tyaktum āviṣṭas tyaktajīvitaḥ prāpnotīndrasya sālokyaṃ śūraḥ pṛṣṭham adarśayan
english: Every warrior, resolved to strike down the foe and ready to cast away his life—the brave man who never shows his back—attains to dwelling in the world of Indra.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ke lokā yudhyamānānāṃ śūrāṇām anivartinām bhavanti nidhanaṃ prāpya tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: What worlds belong to brave warriors who fight without ever turning back, once they have met their end? Tell me that, O grandfather.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam ambarīṣasya saṃvādam indrasya ca yudhiṣṭhira
english: Bhīṣma said: On this too they recount an ancient tale, the dialogue of Ambarīṣa and Indra, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: ambarīṣo hi nābhāgaḥ svargaṃ gatvā sudurlabham dadarśa suralokasthaṃ śakreṇa sacivaṃ saha
english: For Ambarīṣa, son of Nābhāga, having reached that heaven so hard to win, beheld dwelling in the world of the gods, alongside Śakra, his own minister—

sanskrit: sarvatejomayaṃ divyaṃ vimānavaram āsthitam upary upari gacchantaṃ svaṃ vai senāpatiṃ prabhum
english: his own lord and commander-in-chief, formed all of radiance, seated in a splendid celestial chariot, rising higher and higher.

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvopari gacchantaṃ senāpatim udāradhīḥ ṛddhiṃ dṛṣṭvā sudevasya vismitaḥ prāha vāsavam
english: Seeing his commander rising above him, that noble-minded one, beholding the glory of Sudeva, spoke in wonder to Vāsava:

sanskrit: sāgarāntāṃ mahīṃ kṛtsnām anuśiṣya yathāvidhi cāturvarṇye yathāśāstraṃ pravṛtto dharmakāmyayā
english: "Having ruled the whole earth bounded by the sea, in due order, governing the four orders according to scripture, devoted out of love for dharma;

sanskrit: brahmacaryeṇa ghoreṇa ācāryakulasevayā vedān adhītya dharmeṇa rājaśāstraṃ ca kevalam
english: having through stern chastity and service in the teacher's house studied the Vedas in the way of dharma, and the science of kingship complete;

sanskrit: atithīn annapānena pitṝṃś ca svadhayā tathā ṛṣīn svādhyāyadīkṣābhir devān yajñair anuttamaiḥ
english: having honored guests with food and drink, the ancestors with offerings, the seers with private study and consecrations, and the gods with unsurpassed sacrifices;

sanskrit: kṣatradharme sthito bhūtvā yathāśāstraṃ yathāvidhi udīkṣamāṇaḥ pṛtanāṃ jayāmi yudhi vāsava
english: and standing firm in the dharma of the kṣatriya, as scripture and rule prescribe, surveying the host I conquer in battle, O Vāsava—

sanskrit: devarāja sudevo 'yaṃ mama senāpatiḥ purā āsīd yodhaḥ praśāntātmā so 'yaṃ kasmād atīva mām
english: O king of the gods, this Sudeva, who was once my commander, a warrior of serene spirit—why does he so far surpass me?

sanskrit: nānena kratubhir mukhyair iṣṭaṃ naiva dvijātayaḥ tarpitā vidhivac chakra so 'yaṃ kasmād atīva mām
english: He sacrificed not with the foremost rites, nor were the twice-born duly satisfied by him, O Śakra—why then does he so far surpass me?"

sanskrit: indra uvāca etasya vitatas tāta sudevasya babhūva ha saṃgrāmayajñaḥ sumahān yaś cānyo yudhyate naraḥ
english: Indra said: Of this Sudeva, my son, a mighty battle-sacrifice was spread out—as it is for any other man who fights.

sanskrit: saṃnaddho dīkṣitaḥ sarvo yodhaḥ prāpya camūmukham yuddhayajñādhikārastho bhavatīti viniścayaḥ
english: It is settled doctrine that every warrior, armored and consecrated, having reached the front of the host, stands invested with the office of the battle-sacrifice.

sanskrit: ambarīṣa uvāca kāni yajñe havīṃṣy atra kim ājyaṃ kā ca dakṣiṇā ṛtvijaś cātra ke proktās tan me brūhi śatakrato
english: Ambarīṣa said: What are the oblations in this sacrifice, what the clarified butter, and what the fee? And who are called the officiating priests here? Tell me that, O Śatakratu.

sanskrit: indra uvāca ṛtvijaḥ kuñjarās tatra vājino 'dhvaryavas tathā havīṃṣi paramāṃsāni rudhiraṃ tv ājyam eva ca
english: Indra said: There the elephants are the officiating priests, the horses the adhvaryu priests; the choicest flesh is the oblation, and the blood is the clarified butter.

sanskrit: sṛgālagṛdhrakākolāḥ sadasyās tatra satriṇaḥ ājyaśeṣaṃ pibanty ete haviḥ prāśnanti cādhvare
english: The jackals, vultures, and ravens are the assessors and partakers of the session; these drink the remnant of the butter and consume the oblation in that sacrifice.

sanskrit: prāsatomarasaṃghātāḥ khaḍgaśaktiparaśvadhāḥ jvalanto niśitāḥ pītāḥ srucas tasyātha satriṇaḥ
english: The clusters of barbed darts and lances, the swords, spears, and battle-axes, blazing, sharpened, and burnished—these are the sacrificial ladles of him who holds the session.

sanskrit: cāpavegāyatas tīkṣṇaḥ parakāyāvadāraṇaḥ ṛjuḥ suniśitaḥ pītaḥ sāyako 'sya sruvo mahān
english: The arrow, sped by the force of the bow, keen, cleaving the bodies of the foe, straight, well-whetted, and burnished—that is his great offering-spoon.

sanskrit: dvīpicarmāvanaddhaś ca nāgadantakṛtatsaruḥ hastihastagataḥ khaḍgaḥ sphyo bhavet tasya saṃyuge
english: The sword bound with leopard-hide, its hilt wrought of ivory, grasped in a hand strong as an elephant's trunk—that becomes his wooden sword of the rite in the battle.

sanskrit: jvalitair niśitaiḥ pītaiḥ prāsaśaktiparaśvadhaiḥ śaikyāyasamayais tīkṣṇair abhighāto bhaved vasu
english: The smiting with the blazing, whetted, burnished darts, spears, and axes, keen and forged of well-tempered iron—that is his wealth of oblation.

sanskrit: āvegād yat tu rudhiraṃ saṃgrāme syandate bhuvi sāsya pūrṇāhutir hotre samṛddhā sarvakāmadhuk
english: And the blood that, by the rush of onset, streams upon the ground in battle—that is his full and abundant final oblation poured into the fire, yielding every desire.

sanskrit: chindhi bhindhīti yasyaitac chrūyate vāhinīmukhe sāmāni sāmagās tasya gāyanti yamasādane
english: He at the front of whose host this cry is heard, "Cut! Cleave!"—for him the chanters sing the Sāman hymns in the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: havirdhānaṃ tu tasyāhuḥ pareṣāṃ vāhinīmukham kuñjarāṇāṃ hayānāṃ ca varmiṇāṃ ca samuccayaḥ agniḥ śyenacito nāma tasya yajñe vidhīyate
english: They call the front of the enemy's host his oblation-shed; the massed array of elephants, horses, and armored men—that is the fire named Śyenacit, ordained in his sacrifice.

sanskrit: uttiṣṭhati kabandho 'tra sahasre nihate tu yaḥ sa yūpas tasya śūrasya khādiro 'ṣṭāśrir ucyate
english: And the headless trunk that rises up here when a thousand have been slain—that is called the eight-cornered sacrificial post of khadira-wood for that hero.

sanskrit: iḍopahūtaṃ krośanti kuñjarā aṅkuśeritāḥ vyāghuṣṭatalanādena vaṣaṭkāreṇa pārthiva udgātā tatra saṃgrāme trisāmā dundubhiḥ smṛtaḥ
english: The elephants, goaded by the hook, trumpet the call of the Iḍā invocation; with the resounding clap of palms and the cry of Vaṣaṭ, O king, the war-drum sounding its triple Sāman is held to be the chanting priest in that battle.

sanskrit: brahmasve hriyamāṇe yaḥ priyāṃ yuddhe tanuṃ tyajet ātmānaṃ yūpam ucchritya sa yajño 'nantadakṣiṇaḥ
english: He who, when the property of brāhmaṇas is being carried off, gives up his beloved body in battle, raising his own self as the sacrificial post—his is a sacrifice of boundless fee.

sanskrit: bhartur arthe tu yaḥ śūro vikramed vāhinīmukhe bhayān na ca nivarteta tasya lokā yathā mama
english: The brave man who, for his lord's sake, would show his prowess at the front of the host and would not turn back through fear—his worlds are even as mine.

sanskrit: nīlacandrākṛtaiḥ khaḍgair bāhubhiḥ parighopamaiḥ yasya vedir upastīrṇā tasya lokā yathā mama
english: He whose sacrificial altar is strewn over with swords shaped like the dark moon and with arms like iron clubs—his worlds are even as mine.

sanskrit: yas tu nāvekṣate kaṃ cit sahāyaṃ vijaye sthitaḥ vigāhya vāhinīmadhyaṃ tasya lokā yathā mama
english: He who, bent on victory, looks to no comrade for aid and plunges into the very midst of the host—his worlds are even as mine.

sanskrit: yasya tomarasaṃghāṭā bherīmaṇḍūkakacchapā vīrāsthiśarkarā durgā māṃsaśoṇitakardamā
english: He for whom the clustered lances are the rafts, the kettle-drums the frogs and turtles, the bones of heroes the gravel, hard to ford, its mire flesh and blood—

sanskrit: asicarmaplavā sindhuḥ keśaśaivalaśādvalā aśvanāgarathaiś caiva saṃbhinnaiḥ kṛtasaṃkramā
english: a river whose rafts are swords and shields, whose moss and water-grass is human hair, bridged over with shattered horses, elephants, and chariots;

sanskrit: patākādhvajavānīrā hatavāhanavāhinī śoṇitodā susaṃpūrṇā dustarā pāragair naraiḥ
english: its reeds and rushes banners and standards, its current a stream of slain mounts, its waters blood, brimful, hard to cross even for men who would reach the farther shore;

sanskrit: hatanāgamahānakrā paralokavahāśivā ṛṣṭikhaḍgadhvajānūkā gṛdhrakaṅkavaḍaplavā
english: with slain elephants for its great crocodiles, dreadful, bearing men to the other world, its sandbanks heaped with pikes, swords, and standards, with vultures and herons floating upon it—
